# Built Apple II files

Everything here is generated by `software/build.py` and `software/mkdisk.py`; don't edit by hand.
For what the programs do and how to install them, see `software/README.md`.

## The disk image
**`LASERCLOCK.po`**: 140K ProDOS 8 disk (volume `/LASERCLOCK`, ProDOS-order `.po`). This is the one file
most people need. Write it to a 5.25" floppy with ADTPro, or open it in CiderPress, AppleCommander or an
emulator, then copy its files to your boot disk. It holds all of these:

| File | ProDOS type | Load address | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CLOCK.SYSTEM` | SYS ($FF) | $2000 | 1103 | Startup program: finds the card, installs the clock driver (aux-memory copy), then runs `BASIC.SYSTEM`. Goes before `BASIC.SYSTEM` in the boot directory. |
| `CLOCK.MAIN` | BIN ($06) | $6000 | 758 | Installs the main-memory copy of the driver body, in two pages reserved through `BASIC.SYSTEM`. `BRUN` it from `STARTUP`. |
| `CLOCK.SET` | BIN ($06) | $6000 | 314 | Machine-language helper that writes the date and time to the DS3231. Used by `SET.CLOCK`. |
| `CARDTEST` | BIN ($06) | $6000 | 968 | Machine-language test engine (RAM tests, clock test, bank-hop test). Used by `CARD.TEST`. |
| `SET.CLOCK` | BAS ($FC) | $0801 | — | Applesoft program: asks for the date and time and sets the clock. |
| `CARD.TEST` | BAS ($FC) | $0801 | — | Applesoft program: the card test menu. |
| `STARTUP` | BAS ($FC) | $0801 | — | Example startup: `10 PRINT CHR$(4);"BRUN CLOCK.MAIN"`. |

## The loose binaries
`CLOCK.SYSTEM`, `CLOCK.MAIN`, `CLOCK.SET` and `CARDTEST` are also here as raw binaries (no file header), the
same bytes as on the disk. They're for tools that add files to an image one at a time. When adding them by
hand, set the ProDOS type and load (aux) address from the table above. The three BASIC programs exist only
on the disk image, because they are stored tokenised; their source listings are in `software/basic/`.

## Checking
`mkdisk.py` reads the finished image back and compares every file's type, load address and contents.
`software/test/CheckImage.java` does the same check with AppleCommander, independently of our own disk
code (see `software/README.md`).
